question: Whether CCI's current material contradiction set is genuinely mutually exclusive, or instead reflects compatible differences between balance-sheet resilience, AFFO mechanics, customer-specific churn, carrier concentration, and long-run network demand.
whyItMatters: CCI is packet_ready and blocked only by unresolved_material_contradiction. Existing Alpha underwriting is complete and source-addressed, so Resolver can adjudicate the contradiction without taking over underwriting.

items.claimA: Balance-sheet simplification, debt reduction, cost savings and lower financing burden improve resilience and can support AFFO.
items.claimB: 2026 site-rental revenue outlook remains below 2025 actual revenue because DISH terminations, Sprint cancellations and related revenue mechanics outweigh underlying organic contribution.
items.resolutionRule: Claims are resolved as non-mutually-exclusive when current primary evidence attributes them to different economic drivers or scopes; preserve the underlying risks as non-gating.

resolution: The material contradiction set is not mutually exclusive on the current primary record. Crown Castle's 2026 outlook shows site-rental revenue below 2025 actual revenue while underlying organic contribution excluding major tenant cancellation effects remains positive. Separately, the fiber divestiture, large debt repayment, cost reductions and lower interest burden improve financial resilience, while Q2 2026 guidance shows AFFO can increase even as site-rental revenue remains lower year over year. Long-duration contracts can coexist with high carrier concentration, and broad network-demand growth can coexist with company-specific churn. These are scope and driver distinctions rather than conflicting facts. Preserve tenant concentration, cancellation exposure, reduced diversification and architecture substitution as material non-gating risks.
falsifiers: New primary evidence showing the same CCI revenue measure, same period and same customer set simultaneously increasing and decreasing without a reconciliation.
New evidence showing debt reduction or AFFO improvement was asserted to eliminate tenant-cancellation revenue pressure rather than offset it through different financial drivers.
New evidence showing long-duration contract visibility was asserted to eliminate counterparty concentration risk.
